$comment: Documents test-e2e-deploy.yml's NEXTJS_REF (the Next.js ref every compat cell tests) versus packages/kn-next/templates/app/package.json.hbs's next pin (the Next.js version the scaffold actually ships). tests/nextjs-credential-lockstep.test.ts fails if either real value drifts from what THIS file documents, so a future bump to either side must update this manifest in the same PR — a reviewed decision, never silent drift. As of rc.2's 16.3.5 re-credential the two are EQUAL (no more deliberate divergence) — see divergenceReason for the history and what closed it.
divergenceReason: rc.2's 16.3.5 re-credential (#1560, 2026-09-30) closes the divergence rc.1 opened: NEXTJS_REF moves from v16.2.12 to v16.3.5, matching the scaffold's shipped pin. What made this possible: the six deterministic v16.3.5 failures on the four credential cells (five from the #1547/#1570 re-audit, plus one more — a webpack-only Pages API routes rewrite-query case) were triaged and found to be the vercel-infra-coupled family (ADR-0007 §h addendum) — each failing assertion sits in the test's isNextDeploy deploy branch and encodes behaviour only Vercel's own infrastructure produces, with knext's result matching the self-hosted expectation in every case — so they are evidence-quarantined, not knext gaps. Separately, the pre-existing per-case quarantine ledger (14 entries: 12 runtime-prefetch + 2 bun-edge-fetch) was re-audited with REAL dispatch evidence at v16.3.5 (all four credential cells, node/bun x turbopack/webpack, each 16/16 shards, 0 failed): the 12 runtime-prefetch entries all passed cleanly on first attempt (no retry) on all four cells and are REMOVED from the ledger — their cited root-cause fix (vercel/next.js PR #95301, merge commit 97b71d0) is confirmed via the GitHub compare API to be an ancestor of v16.3.5 (compare v16.3.5...97b71d0 -> status 'behind', ahead_by 0) but NOT of v16.2.12 (status 'diverged'), which is why they were still red at the old ref and clean at the new one. The 2 bun-edge-fetch entries also ran clean on both bun cells this time, but their documented mechanism is a Bun-runtime edge-sandbox gap independent of the Next.js ref (Bun build unchanged: 1.4.2 both times) and their own history is 'cross-run wobble' (sometimes green, sometimes red) — a single clean run does not retire that class of entry, so both are RE-STAMPED (reaudited: v16.3.5), not removed, consistent with how they were handled at the v16.2.12 rc.1 audit. History: founder decision 2026-09-27 (#1570) cut rc.1 on v16.2.12 (the latest 16.2.x tag at or above the CVE floor 16.2.11) as the rc.1 rehearsal, deliberately deferring the harder 16.3.5 jump to rc.2 because of five upstream tests added after 16.2.x (run ids 36332940411/36332946048/36332951393/36332959885, PR #1547) — those five are the vercel-infra-coupled entries closed above. The rc.1 bump itself (v16.2.0 -> v16.2.12) was a same-minor-line re-audit of the same 14 entries (run ids on issue #1570 — runs 36348520937/36348526494/36348532038/36348537247), done in that PR, not pending.

lockstepExceptions.reason: The vinext/bun single-executable compat lane (ADR-0048, #608) is a SEPARATE axis from the four node/bun x turbopack/webpack credential cells this manifest tracks — its own credentialing is v1.x scope (not rc.1), so it is deliberately left at the pre-#1570 ref rather than silently re-pinned by this bump. Re-credential it on its own schedule, not as a side effect of the rc.1 rehearsal.

Same as the dispatch-default exception above (compat-vinext.yml) — the vinext lane's NEXTJS_REF env fallback mirrors its own dispatch default and is out of scope for the rc.1 node/bun credential rehearsal (#1570).
